meta.title: Privacy Policy
meta.description: How MCPEmails collects, uses, and protects your data. Our privacy policy for users, workspace owners, and AI agents.

hero.title: Privacy Policy
hero.lead: We built MCPEmails with privacy as a first principle. The email content your agent reads is never stored on our servers; it passes through to your agent and disappears. A few features you turn on keep part of a message for a limited time, such as a message you schedule to send later or a send held for your approval. Section 2.5 lists each one. This policy explains what we do collect, and why.

whoWeAre.title: 1. Who We Are
whoWeAre.p1: The MCPEmails service at mcpemails.com is operated by {companyName}, a Norwegian private limited company (aksjeselskap) owned and run by {ownerName}, trading as "MCPEmails". In this policy, "MCPEmails", "we", "us", and "our" all mean {companyName}. The service includes all dashboard pages, API endpoints, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that AI agents use to access connected email accounts.
whoWeAre.p2: For the purposes of applicable data protection law (including the EU General Data Protection Regulation, "GDPR"), MCPEmails is the data controller for account and usage data. For email content, we act as a data processor on your behalf: we transmit content you authorise us to retrieve, and we do not store it. If you use MCPEmails to process other people's personal data, for example a team's or your customers' mail, our <dpa>Data Processing Agreement</dpa> sets out how we process it on your behalf.
whoWeAre.p3: Service provider identification: {companyName} is a private limited company (aksjeselskap) established in Norway, owned by {ownerName}, who also chairs its board. It is registered in {register}, the Norwegian Register of Business Enterprises operated by Brønnøysundregistrene, under organisation number {orgNumber}. Our registered address is {companyAddress}.
whoWeAre.p4: You can reach us about privacy at <email></email>.

dataWeCollect.title: 2. Data We Collect
dataWeCollect.accountP: When you create an account we collect your email address and a hashed password (we never store plaintext passwords). You may optionally provide a display name. This data is required to create and maintain your account. If you tick the box on the signup form asking for product tips and offers by email, we also record that you did, when, and which wording you saw. When you sign up, we also record whether you used a phone, a tablet, or a computer, worked out from your browser's request headers. We store only that one word, never your browser's user-agent string or any device identifier, and use it only to understand where signups come from. We also record the country a signup came from, as a two-letter code that our hosting provider works out from your IP address. We store only that code, never the IP address, and use it only to understand where signups come from.
dataWeCollect.workspaceP: We store the workspace name you choose, and the configuration of each connected inbox (provider type, email address, OAuth status, and connection timestamp). We do not store OAuth access tokens or app passwords in plaintext. They are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being written to the database, and the encryption key is held as a server secret in our application environment, never in the database.
dataWeCollect.apiKeysP: We store a SHA-256 hash of each API key you create, along with the key's name, scopes, creation timestamp, and last-used timestamp. The raw key value is shown to you exactly once at creation time and is never stored in recoverable form.
dataWeCollect.logsP: For every MCP tool call your agent makes, we record: the tool name (e.g. email_read), the API key that made the call, the inbox that was accessed, the timestamp, and whether the call succeeded. We do not record email subjects, bodies, recipients, or any other email content in these logs.
dataWeCollect.emailContentP: When your agent calls <c>email_read</c> (to list, read, or search) or any other read tool, we fetch the requested content live from your email provider and return it to your agent in the same HTTP response. That content is never written to disk, cached, or logged. Once the HTTP response is sent, we hold no copy of any email body, subject, attachment, or contact detail. A few features need to keep part of a message, and only when you use them. Scheduled sends: we store the outgoing message (recipients, subject, body and attachments), encrypted, until it is sent, and clear its content 7 days after it is sent. Sends held for approval: when an inbox requires approval, a send, reply, forward or draft send your agent requests is stored encrypted until a workspace member approves or rejects it, or until it expires after 24 hours. Its content is cleared 7 days after that decision, and the approval record, with the recipients and subject encrypted, is kept for 90 days as your approval history. Follow-ups and snoozes: we keep the message's subject, sender and recipients, encrypted, until the reminder is done or cancelled. Automations: the run log keeps the sender and the first 120 characters of the subject of each message an automation acted on, for 90 days, so you can see what it did and undo it. Mail your agent reads, and mail it sends immediately without an approval hold, is never stored.
dataWeCollect.emailContentAgentP: Your email content is only ever sent to the MCP client or AI agent that you have connected and are operating (for example Claude, Cursor, or another MCP client of your choosing). When you invoke a tool, MCPEmails transmits the requested content to that client so it can fulfil your request. MCPEmails does not send your email content to any AI provider of its own choosing. Once the content reaches your chosen client, it is governed by that client's or AI provider's own privacy policy and terms, which you are responsible for reviewing. MCPEmails acts only as a conduit and retains no copy of the content. If you set up a webhook (Pro and Business), we also send new-mail notices to the web address you enter. By default a notice carries only message ids; if you choose to include headers, it also carries each new message's sender and subject.
dataWeCollect.technicalP: We collect standard server-side operational data: IP addresses (for rate limiting and abuse prevention), request timestamps, HTTP status codes and error types. When you sign in, connect an AI app, or an AI app renews its access, we also record the IP address and user agent in a security log tied to your account, so you and we can investigate unexpected access. Raw IP addresses and user agents in our security logs are deleted after 30 days; after that only aggregated, anonymised figures remain.
dataWeCollect.cookiesP: We set only first-party cookies, never third-party ones. A session cookie from Supabase Auth keeps you signed in, and <c>mcpe_active_ws</c> remembers which workspace you last opened. Short-lived cookies carry a choice through a sign-in redirect: <c>mcpe_signup_mc</c> (your marketing email choice, 15 minutes) and the Outlook connection cookies, which are deleted when you return. If you arrive through a referral link, <c>mcpe_ref</c> holds the referral code for up to 60 days so the referral can be credited when you sign up. <c>mx_subject</c> is a random id, kept for up to 12 months, that lets us tell whether two visits came from the same browser, so we can measure tests of the website. It is not derived from anything about you and is never shared with advertisers or other websites. If you create an account, we link it to that account to count which version of a page led to the signup. <c>mx_ai_client</c> remembers which AI assistant you came from, for up to 30 days, so the site shows setup steps for it. In your browser's local storage we keep your theme (<c>mcpe-theme</c>), your language (<c>mcpe-locale</c>), how you first reached the site (<c>mcpe-acquisition</c>: a coarse traffic-source category such as <c>reddit</c> or <c>organic_google</c> and the kind of page you landed on, never a search term or a full URL; kept for up to 30 days and saved with your workspace if you sign up) and a few dashboard display preferences. We do not use advertising cookies or cookies that track you across other websites.
dataWeCollect.productAnalyticsP: We use Vercel Web Analytics for privacy-preserving, cookieless product analytics. We measure page visits and a small setup funnel (signup, inbox connection, MCP connection, and first successful tool use) with only documented aggregate categories such as provider, client, connection method, and access profile. We never send email content, addresses, API keys, OAuth tokens, workspace or user IDs, MCP request data, prompts, or mailbox metadata. Vercel's retention and processing details are available at <link>vercel.com/docs/analytics</link>. Vercel Web Analytics sets no cookie. The <c>mx_subject</c> cookie described in section 2.7 is our own and is used only to measure tests of our website.

howWeUseData.title: 3. How We Use Your Data
howWeUseData.intro: We use the data described above for the following purposes:
howWeUseData.providingP: We use your account data to authenticate you, your workspace configuration to route MCP tool calls to the correct email provider, and your API keys to authorise agent requests. Without this data the service cannot function. The legal basis under GDPR is performance of a contract.
howWeUseData.securityP: We use IP addresses, request rates, and error patterns to detect and block abusive activity, enforce rate limits, and protect the availability of the service for all users. The legal basis is our legitimate interests in operating a secure service.
howWeUseData.analyticsP: We use aggregated, anonymised usage data (tool call counts, error rates, latency) to understand how the service is used and to prioritise improvements. Product statistics are aggregated. We use individual account and usage signals to enforce plan limits (section 3.4), to send the setup emails described in section 3.10, to measure tests of our website (section 2.7), to help you when something fails, and, if you opted in, to choose which marketing email to send you (section 3.9). The legal basis is our legitimate interests in improving the service.
howWeUseData.billingP: We use usage counts to determine whether your workspace has reached plan limits and to calculate your invoice on paid plans. The legal basis is performance of a contract.
howWeUseData.legalP: We may process and disclose data where required by applicable law, court order, or regulatory authority. The legal basis is compliance with a legal obligation.
neverList: Sell your personal data or usage data to third parties.
Use your email content for training AI models.
Use your data to serve you advertising.
Share your data with third parties for their own marketing purposes.
howWeUseData.googleP1: MCPEmails' use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs (including the Gmail API) will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
howWeUseData.googleP2: If you connect a Gmail account with Google sign-in (OAuth), you grant MCPEmails the following Gmail scopes. If you connect Gmail with an app password instead, no Google API scope is granted and your mailbox is reached over IMAP and SMTP. We request each scope solely to provide the features you invoke through your AI agent, and we use them only on your behalf:
howWeUseData.googleScopeReadonly: <c>gmail.readonly</c>: list messages and read message contents so your agent can search, read, and summarise email at your request.
howWeUseData.googleScopeSend: <c>gmail.send</c>: compose and send messages that your agent creates at your request.
howWeUseData.googleScopeModify: <c>gmail.modify</c>: organise your mail at your direction, including applying and removing labels, marking messages read or unread, archiving messages, moving messages between folders, and moving messages to trash.
howWeUseData.googleScopeSettings: <c>gmail.settings.basic</c>: read your Gmail "Send mail as" addresses and the signature set for them, so your agent can send from an alias Google has already verified for you, with your Gmail signature. We only read these settings and never change them.
howWeUseData.googleLimitedIntro: Consistent with the Limited Use requirements, MCPEmails:
googleLimitedList: uses Google user data only to provide and improve the user-facing features described above;
does not transfer or sell Google user data to third parties, data brokers, or advertising networks;
does not use Google user data for serving advertisements;
does not use Google user data to develop, improve, or train generalised or non-personalised AI or machine-learning models;

does not allow humans to read Google user data unless (a) you give explicit consent for specific messages, (b) it is necessary for security purposes such as investigating abuse, (c) it is required to comply with applicable law, or (d) the data has been aggregated and anonymised.
howWeUseData.googleP3: Apart from the few feature records listed in section 2.5, email content retrieved from the Gmail API is streamed through to your agent in the same request and is never stored, cached, or logged by MCPEmails.
howWeUseData.microsoftTitle: 3.8 Microsoft APIs: mailbox access and revoking it
howWeUseData.microsoftP1: When you connect an Outlook or Microsoft 365 mailbox, Microsoft asks you to approve a specific, named set of permissions: reading and organising your mail, and sending mail on your behalf. We use that access only to run the features you ask an AI agent to perform on your mailbox, such as reading, searching, organising, drafting and sending. We do not use it to build a copy of your mailbox, and we never use mail content, or anything derived from it, for advertising or marketing.
howWeUseData.microsoftRevokeP: You can withdraw this access at any time, directly with Microsoft and without asking us. For a personal Microsoft account, use <personal>Microsoft account permissions</personal>. For a work or school account, use <work>My Apps</work>. Revoking access there immediately stops us being able to reach that mailbox. If your IT admin approved MCPEmails for your whole organisation, only an admin can remove that organisation-wide approval.
howWeUseData.microsoftDisconnectP: Disconnecting the inbox in your MCPEmails dashboard has the same effect from our side and additionally deletes the stored credentials for that mailbox. You can do either one first; you do not have to do both.
howWeUseData.marketingP1: We send marketing email (product tips and offers, for example about a paid plan when your workspace reaches a plan limit) only if you agreed to it by ticking the box on the signup form. The box is unticked by default, and we do not infer consent from anything else. The legal basis is your consent (GDPR Article 6(1)(a)), which the Norwegian Marketing Control Act (markedsføringsloven) § 15 also requires for marketing by email.
howWeUseData.marketingP2: To choose which of a small number of messages to send, and when, we use account and product-usage signals: for example that your workspace reached a plan limit, how many inboxes you have connected, your plan, and when you signed up. We never use the content of your mailbox, or anything derived from it, for this.
howWeUseData.marketingP3: You can withdraw your consent at any time with the unsubscribe link in every marketing email. It takes effect immediately and does not affect receipts, security notices, or other email we need to send to run your account. We keep a record of when you consented and which wording you saw, so that we can show consent was given.
howWeUseData.setupHelpTitle: 3.10 Emails to help you finish setting up
howWeUseData.setupHelpP: If you start setting up MCPEmails and get stuck, we may send you up to two short emails to help you finish: for example after a failed connection, with the fix for the error we saw, or after you connected an inbox but have not used it from your AI app yet. To choose which email to send and when, we use the setup steps recorded for your workspace, such as which provider failed and why and which AI app you picked. We never use the content of your mailbox for this, and these emails contain no offers. The legal basis is our legitimate interests in helping you use the service you signed up for. Every one of these emails has an unsubscribe link, which stops them immediately.

dataRetention.title: 4. Data Retention
dataRetention.intro: We keep each category of data for the following periods:

rows.category: Marketing email consent and unsubscribe record

rows.period: Until deleted by you, plus 30 days
Until inbox disconnected or account deleted
rows.reason: Required to authenticate provider API calls

rows.period: Free: shown for 30 days, stored for 90. Personal: 90 days. Pro and Business: 2 years
rows.reason: Security; usage history in your dashboard

rows.category: Server and security logs (IP address, user agent, status)
Email content your agent reads or sends immediately

rows.period: Until sent, then 7 days; the message content is then cleared
rows.reason: Required to deliver messages you schedule

rows.period: Encrypted while waiting for a decision (at most 24 hours) and for 7 days after it; the approval record (recipients and subject, encrypted) is kept 90 days
rows.reason: Required to show the message to a reviewer and send it once approved

rows.category: Follow-ups and snoozes (subject, sender, recipients, encrypted)
rows.period: Until the reminder is done or cancelled
rows.reason: Required to check for a reply and to list the reminder

rows.category: Automation run log (sender, first 120 characters of the subject)
rows.reason: Showing and undoing what an automation did

dataRetention.outro: When you delete your account, we immediately delete the stored passwords and tokens for every connected inbox, revoke your Google grants, API keys and AI app connections, and block sign-in. Within 30 days we erase everything else tied to the account: account and workspace records, inbox settings, the activity log, scheduled and approved send history, and messages you sent to support. Deleted data can remain in encrypted database backups for up to 7 more days, after which the backups expire. Aggregated, non-personal statistics may be kept.

thirdParties.title: 5. Third Parties and Data Sharing
thirdParties.infraP: We use the following sub-processors to operate the service. Each processes data only on our instructions and under a data processing agreement or the provider's standard data processing terms. For customers who process other people's personal data through MCPEmails, our <dpa>Data Processing Agreement</dpa> covers this processing:
thirdParties.supabaseData: Account data, workspace config, audit logs; email content passes through live and is stored only as section 2.5 describes
thirdParties.supabaseLocation: Data stored in the EU (Stockholm, Sweden). Edge functions run in the US (East) and process email live
thirdParties.vercelData: HTTP request metadata; MCP requests and responses, including email content, pass through in transit and are not stored
thirdParties.vercelLocation: Global CDN; server functions in the US (East) and the EU (Stockholm, Sweden)
thirdParties.relayPurpose: Mail relay for the few providers that refuse connections from cloud addresses
thirdParties.relayData: The encrypted IMAP and SMTP connection to those providers, passed through as a tunnel with TLS end to end: the relay cannot read mail or passwords
thirdParties.resendPurpose: Sending account, billing and support email, and marketing email if you opted in
thirdParties.resendData: Your email address and name, and the content of the emails we send you, including support confirmations that repeat your message. Never your mailbox content
thirdParties.migaduPurpose: Hosting our own mailboxes: the support mailbox and the noreply address that sends sign-up and password emails
thirdParties.migaduData: Your email address, the sign-up and password emails we send you, and what you write to support
thirdParties.stripeData: Billing email, payment card data (stored by Stripe, not us)
thirdParties.emailProvidersP: When you connect Gmail, Outlook / Microsoft 365, Fastmail, or another IMAP account, MCPEmails authenticates with that provider using credentials you supply. Your email provider's own privacy policy governs the data held in your mailbox. MCPEmails reaches your mailbox when your agent makes a tool call, and in the background only for features you turn on: scheduled sends, automations, follow-ups and snoozes, the morning brief, and new-mail webhooks. Each reads only what that feature needs.
thirdParties.noBrokersTitle: 5.3 No data brokers or advertising networks
thirdParties.noBrokersP: We do not share any data with data brokers, advertising networks, social media platforms, or analytics companies that build user profiles.
thirdParties.legalDisclosuresP: We may disclose personal data if required by law, valid legal process (such as a court order or subpoena), or to protect the rights, property, or safety of MCPEmails, our users, or the public. Where permitted by law, we will notify affected users before disclosing their data.
thirdParties.businessTransfersP: In the event of a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, personal data may be transferred as part of that transaction. We will notify users via the email address on their account before any such transfer occurs and before their data becomes subject to a different privacy policy.

internationalTransfers.title: 6. International Data Transfers
internationalTransfers.p1: MCPEmails is operated from Norway, which is subject to the European Economic Area (EEA) data protection framework. If you access the service from outside the EEA, your data may be transferred to and processed in countries within the EEA.
internationalTransfers.p2: Our sub-processors based in the US (Supabase, Vercel and Resend) operate under Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission for data transfers to third countries. For Stripe, processing is covered by their EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification. Hetzner processes data in Germany and Migadu in Switzerland, which the European Commission recognises as providing adequate protection.
internationalTransfers.p3: Our database, which holds account and configuration data, is hosted in the EU (Stockholm, Sweden) for every customer. There is no plan or setting that moves it to another region. Not every server that handles your agent's requests is in the EU: the edge functions that connect to your mailbox run in the United States (US East), and so does the part of our website that relays those requests. Email content passes through them live, to answer the request, and is not stored there. Encrypted credentials are decrypted in that same US environment for the duration of a request.

yourRights.title: 7. Your Rights
yourRights.intro: Depending on your location, you may have the following rights regarding your personal data:

rights.desc: Request a copy of all personal data we hold about you.
Ask us to correct inaccurate or incomplete data.
Request deletion of your personal data. You can trigger this yourself by deleting your account in Dashboard → Settings → Delete Account.
Ask us to restrict processing of your data in certain circumstances.
Request your data in a machine-readable format (JSON). We provide the export on request; there is no self-serve export tool.
Object to processing based on legitimate interests.
Where processing is based on consent, withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of prior processing.

yourRights.exercise: To exercise any of these rights, email us at <email></email>. We will respond within one month (or 72 hours for urgent security-related requests). We may ask you to verify your identity before processing the request.
yourRights.complaint: If you are located in the EEA or UK, you have the right to lodge a complaint with your local supervisory authority. In Norway, this is the Datatilsynet (datatilsynet.no).

security.title: 8. Security
security.intro: We take the security of your data seriously and implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, including:
measures: All data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. Connections that do not support TLS are rejected.

OAuth tokens and IMAP credentials are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. The encryption key is held as a server secret in our application environment, separate from the database, and is never stored alongside the encrypted data.
API keys are hashed with SHA-256 before storage. The raw key cannot be recovered from the hash.
Database access is protected by Row-Level Security (RLS) policies that prevent one workspace from accessing another's data, even in the event of a query logic error.
Administrative access to production infrastructure requires multi-factor authentication and is logged.
security.reportP: Despite these measures, no system is perfectly secure. If you discover a security vulnerability, please report it responsibly to <securityEmail></securityEmail>. We aim to acknowledge reports within 24 hours and resolve confirmed vulnerabilities within 72 hours for critical issues.
security.breachP: If a personal data breach is likely to result in a risk to your rights and freedoms, we will notify the relevant supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, as GDPR Article 33 requires. Where the risk to you is high, we will also notify affected users without undue delay, as Article 34 requires.

children.title: 9. Children's Privacy
children.p: MCPEmails is not directed at children under the age of 16. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 16. If you believe we have inadvertently collected data from a child, please contact us at <email></email> and we will delete it promptly.

changes.title: 10. Changes to This Policy
changes.intro: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. When we make material changes (such as collecting new categories of data or sharing data with new third parties) we will:
list: Update the "Last updated" date at the top of this page.
Send an email notification to the address registered on your account at least 14 days before the changes take effect.
Display a prominent notice in the dashboard for 14 days after the change takes effect.
changes.outro: Your continued use of the service after a change takes effect constitutes acceptance of the updated policy. If you disagree with a material change, you may delete your account before the effective date.

contact.title: 11. Contact Us
contact.intro: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, wish to exercise a data subject right, or want to report a privacy concern, please contact us:
contact.responseValue: We respond to all privacy requests within one month

cta.title: Questions about your data?
cta.sub: Email us about anything in this policy and we will respond within one month.
